description: Conversion of dwelling into four flats (3 X 1 bed, 1 X 2 bed); single storey rear extension; rear patio with steps; first floor roof terrace; landscaping; parking; bin/cycle stores; external alterations (Demolition of two outbuildings and canopy in rear garden)
decision_conditions: <p>The proposed conversion of the dwellinghouse into four flats, by reason of the excessive number of occupiers that it will accommodates together with the poor standard of layout of the flats cumulating from the poor outlook from and natural light to the bedrooms serving flats 1, 2 and 3, substandard private amenity for flat 1 and the lack of private amenity for flat 4 and the conflict in vertical stacking between flats 2 and 3, and failure to meet the minimum internal space standards with respect to flats 1 and 3 would result in an overly intensive use of the site and give rise to a poor standard of living accommodation for the future occupiers of the development to the detriment of the living conditions of the future occupiers of the site. The development is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policies D3 and D6 The London Plan (2021), Policies DM1, DM26 and DM27 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013), the Mayor of London Supplementary Planning Guidance Housing (2016), and the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p>The proposed roof terrace by reason of its positioning would result in noise disturbance and overlooking and would be detrimental to the residential amenities of the occupiers of neighbouring properties, contrary to Policy D3.D (1) and (11) of The London Plan (2021), Core Policy CS1B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM1 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and the adopted Supplementary Planning Document Residential Design Guide (2010).&nbsp;</p>

<p>The cumulative impacts of the proposed car parking space and bin stores together with the required number of secure and sheltered cycle spaces that would be required to serve the development cannot be satisfactorily provided within the curtilage of the site to meet the Council's requirements in respect of the development, and the likely increase in such allocated spaces for cycles on the front forecourt of the property would leave limited scope for sufficient soft landscaping to mitigate the impact of the development in the wider area. This will result in visual clutter which will be detrimental to the character and appearance of the area. The proposal also in the absence of providing the required number of cycle spaces needed to serve the development would fail to promote sustainable transport. The proposal is therefore contrary to National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policies D3 and T6 of The London Plan (2021), Policy CS.1 of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and Policies DM1, DM22 and DM42 of the Development Management Plan Local Policies (2013).</p>
